issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Farm.addAnimal(animal: Animal): boolean (a boolean return type), while the solution implements addAnimal as void and the template Farm.java does not provide the method (the main usage in Main assumes no return value). The problem statement text describing addAnimal does not mention a boolean return either, creating a contradiction between the UML and the implementation expectations. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected signature and return type for addAnimal.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the expected signature explicit and consistent: either update the UML in the problem statement to declare addAnimal(animal: Animal): void (matching the solution and typical usage), or change the solution/template to implement addAnimal to return boolean. Also update the textual description to state the chosen return type so students know which signature to implement.
